plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other rational bidders do. If I underbid, I risk losing auctions I should win; if I overbid, I risk winning at a price above my value. Since my value is $40, I should bid exactly $40, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $13, I should bid exactly $13 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win only when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to you; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, regardless of Andy and Betty's strategies or beliefs about me, my optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $17.
